explanations: luna: The section’s root ن ع م is present in “those You have favored,” and the same verse distinguishes their path from the paths of anger and error. That joins favor with guidance, as the surah’s progression from being lost to being guided does. | terra: The straight path is identified as the path of those upon whom God has bestowed favor; favor and guidance are inseparable in the Quran's opening prayer.

luna: The section treats the final, better outcome as a completed divine favor. In this ayah, the change of prayer direction is followed by “that I may complete My favor upon you,” with guidance as the surrounding purpose; this is another concrete completion of favor through a directed course. | terra: God makes direction toward the Sacred Mosque serve two stated ends, وَلِأُتِمَّ نِعْمَتِي عَلَيْكُمْ and guidance; this is another explicit completion-of-favor and path pairing.
terra: The Messenger's reciting, purifying, and teaching supplies the staged means by which the favor and guidance promised in 2:150 reach the community.
terra: Immediately after the completed-favor passage, God commands remembrance and gratitude and forbids ingratitude; it states the recipient's answer to the completed gift.
terra: Believers are commanded to eat the good things God provided and thank Him; delivered good becomes the immediate ground of gratitude.
terra: Whoever changes God's favor after it has reached them faces severe consequence; the ayah marks reception as no guarantee against corrupting the gift.

luna: The section’s dictionary gloss says khayr is what everyone desires. This ayah supplies a specific boundary: people may dislike what is good for them and love what is bad, so immediate desire does not define the good promised in the section. | terra: People may dislike what is good for them and love what is bad while God knows and they do not; it sets an epistemic boundary on reading present conditions as favor or harm.
terra: The believers are told to remember God's favor and the Book and wisdom sent to instruct them; favor includes an ongoing guidance that must be recollected after receipt.
terra: Mothers nurse for two complete years for one who wants to complete nursing, while the father must provide fairly; child-rearing is portrayed as care, provision, and an intended completion.
terra: A goodly loan to God is multiplied many times; benefit advanced to another returns as divinely increased good.

luna: The section’s dictionary example for root ر ب ب is tending a plot of land and bringing it to sound completion. This ayah stages a seed growing into many ears and multiplies the return on charitable giving, joining the land image to an increase in good passed onward. | terra: A benefit passed onward is pictured as a seed producing seven ears and seven hundred grains, after which God multiplies further; cultivation and increase explain how given good grows.

luna: The section’s land-care dictionary sense meets this parable of spending as a garden on high ground, whose yield doubles after rain. It makes a cultivated plot the image of a good act that grows into more provision.
terra: God destroys usury and causes charities to grow; the ayah directly distinguishes extractive increase from increase attached to conveyed good.

luna: The section explains riḍwān as abundant approval. This ayah names gardens and “approval from Allah” among what is better for the God-conscious, making divine approval part of the better gift beyond worldly desire. | terra: “Shall I tell you of something better than that?” leads from worldly desires to gardens and رِضْوَانٌ مِنَ اللَّهِ; what is truly better culminates in abundant approval.

luna: The section’s dictionary account of Rabb includes bringing care to completion. This ayah says Mary’s Lord accepted her well, “grew her with a good growth,” and provided her sustenance; it shows divine care as a developing, sustained provision. | terra: God accepts Mary graciously, causes her to grow a good growth, assigns her to Zechariah, and repeatedly provides for her; child-rearing, cultivation, and provision merge in one sustained care.

terra: The believers are commanded to remember God's favor when hostility became brotherhood and when He rescued them from the brink of the Fire; the favor is a narrated transformation from one state to another.

luna: This ayah says Allah favored the believers by sending them a messenger who recites, purifies, and teaches them, after they had been in clear error. It joins favor to the Prophet’s mission and guidance, matching the section’s connection between divine favor and the stages of being guided. | terra: God's favor to the believers is the sending of a messenger who recites, purifies, and teaches them after evident error; the benefit advances them through an ordered sequence of guidance.
terra: The believers return untouched by harm with favor and bounty from God while following His approval; favor, safety, and riḍwān occur together.
terra: People may dislike something in which God places abundant good; present perception therefore does not exhaust the good being brought about.

luna: The section’s lexicon defines inʿām as conveying goodness to another. This ayah makes that transfer specific through commands to do good to parents, relatives, orphans, the needy, neighbors, and travelers.
terra: Referring disputes to God and the Messenger is called better and best in outcome; khayr and taʾwīl meet in an ordered return to the final meaning.

luna: This ayah calls the enjoyment of worldly life little and says the Hereafter is better for the God-conscious. It makes the section’s “better for you than the first” comparison concrete through the contrast in lasting reward. | terra: Worldly enjoyment is called little and the Hereafter better for the reverent; it repeats the section's comparative judgment in a warning against attachment to the near life.
terra: God will fully pay the believers' rewards and وَيَزِيدُهُمْ مِنْ فَضْلِهِ; complete recompense followed by increase is a direct nonlexical rendering of the image's two motions.

luna: The section links completion with the endpoint of contentment. This ayah says “I have completed My favor upon you” and joins that completion to Allah’s approval of Islam as religion, giving a direct Quranic instance of favor reaching a settled end. | terra: أَتْمَمْتُ عَلَيْكُمْ نِعْمَتِي names the favor as completed and immediately joins completion to God's approval of Islam, وَرَضِيتُ; it directly unites the section's completion and riḍā.

luna: The section’s central completion claim meets “that He may complete His favor upon you” here: after ablution and purification, Allah gives a manageable practice and names completion of favor as its purpose. | terra: After the rulings of purification, God says He intends to purify the believers and لِيُتِمَّ نِعْمَتَهُ عَلَيْكُمْ; bodily preparation becomes a concrete form of favor brought to completion.
terra: Believers are told to remember God's favor when hostile people intended to seize them and He restrained their hands; protection from a concrete threat is made a narrated blessing.

luna: The section says the root ر ض و reaches its fullest form in riḍwān and the surah also moves from being lost to guidance. This ayah says the Book guides those who seek Allah’s approval to paths of peace, joining the section’s two details of approval and guidance. | terra: God guides those who seek His approval along paths of peace and out of darkness into light; riḍwān determines the path and its repaired condition.

luna: Moses tells his people to remember Allah’s favor upon them, naming prophets, kings, and gifts they had not received from others. This is a communal instance of the section’s command to make the Lord’s favor known. | terra: Moses commands his people to remember God's favor in making among them prophets and rulers and granting what others lacked; it is communal narration of a favor unfolded through history.

luna: This ayah says the bad and the good are not equal, even if the abundance of bad things impresses someone. It sets a concrete boundary on reading worldly quantity as the khayr that the section associates with the better outcome.

terra: God commands Jesus to remember His favor upon him and his mother, then enumerates support, teaching, miracles, and protection; it models speaking a prophetic life's completed sequence of favors.

luna: This ayah ends the account of the truthful with gardens and Allah’s approval of them, and their approval of Him. It offers another Quranic form of the section’s contentment as the outcome of divine gift.

luna: The section’s claim that the Hereafter is better than the first life is stated here as the Hereafter’s abode being better for those mindful of God; the worldly life is called play and amusement. It gives the comparison a moral boundary. | terra: Worldly life is play and diversion, while the home of the Hereafter is better for the reverent; the better later state is contrasted with passing activity.
terra: After warnings are forgotten, the gates of everything are opened until the recipients exult and are seized suddenly; apparent increase can be a prelude to judgment rather than completed good.

luna: The section’s root entry uses a plot of land as something repaired and brought to completion. This ayah describes rain, grain, palm growth, and gardens emerging from earth, making the land’s productive provision visible. | terra: Rain becomes vegetation, grain, dates, grapes, olives, and pomegranates, and readers are told to look at fruit and its ripening; the scene makes beneficence visible as growth carried to maturity.

luna: The section’s land dictionary sense meets this ayah’s gardens, crops, and harvest; it tells people to eat the produce and give its due on harvest day. The field’s completed yield becomes provision passed on to others.
terra: The Book given to Moses is described as a completion for the one who did good, a detailed exposition, guidance, and mercy; completion and guidance are again aspects of one delivered good.
luna: The section’s entry for ن ع م includes an increase sense. This ayah says a good deed receives ten like it, a specific example of goodness being multiplied rather than merely returned once.
terra: The people of the Garden praise God for guiding them and confess they could not have found the path unless He guided them; completed guidance is narrated by its recipients.

luna: The section’s dictionary entry for ر ب ب includes bringing land into a sound, productive state. This ayah distinguishes good land whose plants emerge by its Lord’s leave from bad land that yields little, making the land’s response to care a concrete scene.

luna: This ayah says “remember Allah’s favor” and then that He “increased you in stature.” The section’s stated dictionary connection between the ن ع م family and increase is made concrete as a granted increase that calls for remembrance. | terra: Hud tells his people to remember being made successors after Noah and being increased in stature, then to remember God's benefits; recalled favor and increase are expressly joined.
terra: Salih's people are told to remember being settled in the land with palaces and mountain homes and to remember God's benefits; habitation and shaped land are favors demanding recognition.
terra: Heirs to scripture grasp the goods of the lower life while presuming forgiveness, then are reminded that the later home is better for the reverent; “better” corrects compromised desire.

luna: The believers are told to remember when they were few, oppressed, and afraid of being seized, then Allah gave them shelter, support, and good provision. This staged movement from vulnerability to safety and provision parallels the section’s shelter, guidance, and sufficiency. | terra: The believers are told to remember being few and vulnerable before God فَآوَاكُمْ, strengthened them, and provided good things so they might thank; its shelter-to-provision sequence closely restages 93:6-8 and ends in gratitude.

luna: This ayah states that Allah does not change a favor bestowed on a people until they change what is within themselves. It gives a boundary to the section’s account of a favor completed by its giver: the people’s response matters to what follows. | terra: God does not change a favor He has bestowed until a people change what is in themselves; completed favor has a moral boundary and may be lost through its recipients' alteration.
terra: Captives are promised that if God knows good in their hearts, He will give them something better than what was taken and forgive them; loss can be carried to a superior divine replacement.
terra: God gives believers glad tidings of mercy, رِضْوَانٍ, and gardens with lasting bliss; abundant approval accompanies the completed good state.

luna: The addressed believers are asked whether they prefer worldly life to the Hereafter, after being called to go forth. It puts the section’s better-after-this-life claim into a direct challenge to the audience’s preference. | terra: Those clinging to the ground are asked whether they are satisfied with worldly life instead of the Hereafter, whose comparison makes present enjoyment very small.
terra: The Prophet is told not to admire opponents' wealth and children because God may punish them through those very things; visible abundance is bounded from true favor.

luna: This ayah places “approval from Allah” above the gardens and dwellings promised to believers. It concretely supports the section’s reading of riḍwān as an especially full contentment that crowns other gifts. | terra: After lasting gardens and dwellings, وَرِضْوَانٌ مِنَ اللَّهِ أَكْبَرُ declares God's abundant approval greater; satisfaction is the surpassing completion of all listed gifts.

luna: This ayah compares worldly life to rain-grown plants that flourish, then become stubble when Allah’s command arrives, though their owners thought they controlled them. The field scene joins the section’s land dictionary sense to its contrast between passing provision and the better lasting outcome.
terra: Those who do good receive الْحُسْنَىٰ وَزِيَادَةٌ, “the best” together with increase; the reward exceeds completion and becomes the good state named by the source's niʿmah definition.

luna: The section says the ن ع م family includes eye-delight and an excellent state. This ayah commands rejoicing in Allah’s bounty and mercy, a specific expression of joy in divine giving. | terra: People are told to rejoice in God's bounty and mercy because it is خَيْرٌ مِمَّا يَجْمَعُونَ; true delight lies in divine good rather than accumulated possessions.
terra: No one can remove harm God touches or repel good He intends, and His bounty reaches whom He wills; the ayah makes both delivery and ownership of good exclusive to God.
terra: When mercy once tasted is removed, the human becomes despairing and ungrateful; it supplies the first mistaken response in the changing-condition sequence continued by 11:10-11.
terra: After hardship is replaced by favor, a person boasts that evils have left him and becomes exultant; the transition is real but its self-satisfied reading is defective.
terra: The patient who do good are excepted from that defective response and receive forgiveness and great reward; endurance turns changing conditions toward a lasting completion.

luna: The section’s dictionary reading of Rabb completes a favor; here Yaʿqub tells the young Yusuf that Allah will complete His favor upon him and the family of Yaʿqub. The future fulfillment makes the section’s gradual movement from gift to completion concrete. | terra: Jacob promises that God will choose Joseph, teach him, and وَيُتِمُّ نِعْمَتَهُ عَلَيْكَ, extending the completed favor to Jacob's household; the blessing is a process whose end embraces a family.
terra: After Joseph's authority and mercy in this world, the reward of the Hereafter is called better for believers; his realized favor remains open to a superior later good.

terra: At recognition Joseph says God has favored him and his brother and links that outcome to reverence and patience; the early promise of completed family favor is acknowledged within its fulfillment.

luna: This ayah supplies the fulfillment side of Yusuf’s forecast in 12:6: he recognizes the old dream as made true and names Allah’s kindness in bringing him from prison and his family from the desert. Its own contribution is the realized outcome of the favor promised to the young Yusuf. | terra: At the reunion Joseph identifies the scene as the تأويل of his old dream, says his Lord made it true, brought him from prison, and gathered his family; the predicted favor has reached its end and collected his affairs.
terra: After the reunion, Joseph recounts the kingdom and dream-knowledge God gave him and addresses God as his guardian in both worlds; received favor is spoken at the story's completed end.

luna: The section’s dictionary entry gives tending and improving a plot of land as a sense of root ر ب ب. This ayah describes neighboring plots, gardens, crops, and palms watered by the same water yet producing different fruits, making the land sense concrete.

luna: This ayah pairs Allah’s expansion and restriction of provision with people rejoicing in worldly life, then calls worldly life only brief enjoyment compared with the Hereafter. It directly links provision’s changing measure to the section’s caution against treating this life as the final good.
terra: Moses tells his people اذْكُرُوا نِعْمَةَ اللَّهِ عَلَيْكُمْ and recounts their rescue from Pharaoh; it models narrating a favor, and the next ayah states its increase through gratitude.

luna: The section’s dictionary entry for root ن ع م gives “anʿama” the sense of increasing. Here Allah promises, “If you are grateful, I will surely increase you,” making gratitude and an increase of favor an explicit relation. | terra: God's promise لَئِن شَكَرْتُمْ لَأَزِيدَنَّكُمْ makes gratitude the condition of increase, precisely realizing the source section's secondary sense “أَنْعَمَ ... زَادَ.”
terra: Those who exchange نِعْمَتَ اللَّهِ كُفْرًا turn favor into ingratitude and lead their people to ruin; it is the destructive reversal of grateful increase in 14:7.

luna: The section’s claim of increasing favor meets this statement that, even if people tried, they could not enumerate Allah’s favor. It supplies the scale of the gift behind the instruction to speak of it. | terra: God gives from everything people ask, and His favor cannot be counted; the completed gifts exceed any finite inventory.
terra: Abraham publicly praises God for granting Ishmael and Isaac in old age; he models speaking of a long-awaited gift after it arrives.
terra: Water sent from the sky becomes drink and vegetation on which animals graze; divine provision begins the estate's movement from water to use.
terra: The same water grows crops, olives, palms, grapes, and every fruit; the cultivated benefit develops into completed variety.

luna: This repeated Quranic formulation says people cannot count Allah’s favors even if they tried. It makes the section’s image of an increasing, completed favor perceptible as abundance beyond enumeration. | terra: وَإِنْ تَعُدُّوا نِعْمَةَ اللَّهِ لَا تُحْصُوهَا makes divine favor uncountable, giving the section's “increase” an abundance beyond enumeration.
terra: Those who answer that their Lord sent good receive good here, and the home of the Hereafter is better; one divine good advances into another superior state.

luna: The section describes a favor as a good condition and an act of conveying goodness, and 93:11 calls it “your Lord’s favor.” This ayah locates every favor that people have in Allah, grounding the command to recount it in its source. | terra: وَمَا بِكُمْ مِنْ نِعْمَةٍ فَمِنَ اللَّهِ gives every favor a single source, grounding the section's claim that the blessing belongs to the Lord who delivers it.

terra: God brings people from their mothers' wombs knowing nothing, gives hearing, sight, and hearts, and states gratitude as the purpose; growth from helplessness into equipped life is a staged favor.

luna: The section’s sense of a favor brought to completion is stated directly in “Thus He completes His favor upon you.” The preceding ayat name shelters, clothing, and protection, so this ayah gathers varied provisions into one completed favor. | terra: After shade, shelters, garments, and armor are enumerated, كَذَٰلِكَ يُتِمُّ نِعْمَتَهُ عَلَيْكُمْ identifies the whole protective sequence as a favor completed toward submission.

luna: The section commands recounting the Lord’s favor; this ayah says people recognize Allah’s favor and then deny it. Its exact “niʿmata Allāh” makes denial the direct opposite of the section’s response to favor. | terra: يَعْرِفُونَ نِعْمَتَ اللَّهِ ثُمَّ يُنْكِرُونَهَا depicts people recognizing God's favor and then denying it, the opposite of the command to tell it truthfully.

luna: The section glosses niʿma as a good condition. This ayah promises a “good life” to a believer who does righteous deeds and a reward according to the best of what they did, a specific account of divinely granted well-being.

luna: This parable says a secure town received abundant provision from every place, then became ungrateful for Allah’s favors and tasted hunger and fear. It directly reverses the section’s good state and increasing favor when the gift is denied. | terra: A secure, tranquil town receives abundant provision from every place, then denies God's favors and is made to taste hunger and fear; the full state of blessing is reversed point by point.

luna: After the account in 16:112–113 of a town that denied Allah’s favor, this ayah commands people to eat good provision and be grateful for Allah’s favor. Its own contribution is the direct pairing of received provision with gratitude. | terra: People are told to eat lawful good provision and to thank God's favor; provision received and gratitude are explicitly paired.

luna: The ayah calls Abraham grateful for Allah’s favors, says Allah chose him, and says He guided him to a straight path. It repeats the section’s specific meeting of favor, gratitude, and guidance in the account of another prophet. | terra: Abraham is شَاكِرًا لِأَنْعُمِهِ; God then chooses him and guides him to a straight path, binding gratitude for favors to selection and guidance.
terra: As the completion of 16:121, God gives Abraham good in this world and places him among the righteous in the Hereafter; the gift spans both temporal sides rather than ending in the first.

luna: This ayah describes someone who seeks the immediate life and hurries toward it, receiving only what Allah wills, before facing Hell. It is a specific boundary to the section’s promise that the later life is better than the first. | terra: One who wants only the immediate life receives whatever God wills and then faces Hell; it begins the contrast that 17:19-21 resolve in favor of the later gift.

luna: This ayah contrasts the previous pursuit of immediate life with the person who seeks the Hereafter and strives for it as a believer, whose effort is appreciated. It gives the better outcome a concrete response and reward. | terra: One who seeks the Hereafter with faithful effort finds that effort appreciated; this identifies the recipient of the better, greater later ranks in 17:21.

terra: كُلًّا نُمِدُّ ... مِنْ عَطَاءِ رَبِّكَ says the Lord continuously extends His gift to both groups and that His giving is not confined; it clarifies the breadth and ongoing delivery in “your Lord will give you.”
terra: After the Lord's unrestricted giving in 17:20, this ayah says the Hereafter is greater in ranks and preference; it gives a measured parallel to the later being better than the first.

luna: The section explicitly says the root ر ب ب includes raising a child but also completing and improving a favor. This prayer recalls parents who “raised me when small” and asks God for mercy on them, placing the ordinary child-rearing sense beside gratitude for care. | terra: رَبَّيَانِي صَغِيرًا uses the رب root for parents raising a small child; it is the exact child-rearing sense from which the source distinguishes the Lord's completing care.
terra: Full measure and a straight balance are called better and best in outcome; completion, right ordering, khayr, and the root of taʾwīl converge in a concrete transaction.
terra: When favor reaches a human, he turns away, and when harm reaches him, he despairs; the paired reactions oppose grateful recognition of the giver.
terra: The garden owner enters his garden wronging himself and says it will never perish; he mistakes a cultivated favor for a self-securing completion.
terra: He doubts the Hour yet assumes he would receive a better return even then; “better” is made to serve entitlement rather than God's promised later good.
terra: His companion says he should have acknowledged “What God wills; no power except through God” upon entering; the proper speech about a garden's blessing is set against boasting.
terra: The fruit is encompassed and the owner wrings his hands over what he spent; the finished garden becomes a ruin when treated as guaranteed possession.

luna: This ayah compares worldly life to rain-grown vegetation that later dries and scatters. The next ayah, 18:46, names worldly wealth and children as adornment and enduring good deeds as better; 18:45 itself contributes the field’s brief flourishing and decay.

luna: The section says khayr is what is desired and the best of things; this ayah contrasts worldly wealth and children with “the enduring good deeds,” which are better with the Lord for reward and hope. It specifies a lasting good rather than a passing possession. | terra: Wealth and children are worldly adornment, while enduring good deeds are better with the Lord in reward and hope; lasting good displaces possession as the desired end.
terra: The two servants intend that the child's parents receive from their Lord a replacement better in purity and nearer in mercy; hidden care may complete itself through a good not yet visible.

luna: This ayah explains that the wall concealed treasure for two orphan boys and that their Lord wanted them to reach maturity and recover it, as mercy from Him. It makes divine shelter and provision for vulnerable children concrete, with the benefit kept for a later stage. | terra: The wall hides treasure for two orphans until they reach maturity, and the explanation says “your Lord willed” that completion as mercy; divine care shelters an orphaned good until its proper end.

luna: Mary is told to eat, drink, and “be comforted in eye” after giving birth. The section’s eye-delight dictionary expression thus appears in another mother-and-child scene, where provision and relief accompany the comfort. | terra: Mary is given water and ripe dates and told to eat, drink, and وَقَرِّي عَيْنًا; provision delivered in distress becomes the source section's “eye's delight.”

terra: وَيَزِيدُ اللَّهُ الَّذِينَ اهْتَدَوْا هُدًى joins increase to guidance, then calls enduring good deeds better with the Lord in reward and return; increase, path, and better outcome form one movement.
terra: God tells Moses that He had bestowed favor on him once before, explicitly introducing the remembered sequence that culminates in the eye-delight and appointed arrival of 20:40.
terra: Inspiring Moses' mother is the first concrete act within the former favor announced in 20:37; the completed rescue begins as hidden direction.
terra: The chest, river, divinely cast love, and rearing under God's eye show protective care operating through danger before the reunion narrated in 20:40.

luna: The section names the dictionary expression “nuʿmatu al-ʿayn,” the eye’s delight, and points to Moses’s return to his mother. This ayah says he was returned to her “so her eye might be comforted,” making the promised favor a mother’s restored child. | terra: Moses is returned to his mother كَيْ تَقَرَّ عَيْنُهَا وَلَا تَحْزَنَ, then rescued, tried, and brought at the appointed time; it supplies both the source's “eye's delight” sense and a long favor completed in stages.

luna: The section’s rida detail has Allah give until the Prophet is content; Moses here says he hurried to his Lord “that You may be pleased.” The direction of seeking approval is reversed, making the mutual relation between gift and contentment visible.
terra: The Prophet is commanded to endure and glorify his Lord through the day's turns so that he may be satisfied; it is another direct divine address promising his satisfaction.
terra: The Prophet is told not to stretch his eyes toward worldly bloom, for وَرِزْقُ رَبِّكَ خَيْرٌ وَأَبْقَى; the Lord's provision is the better, enduring good.
terra: Following 20:131, God says “We do not ask you for provision; We provide you,” and makes the final outcome belong to reverence; the source and endpoint of sufficiency are clarified.
terra: The question asks whether wealth and sons supplied to deniers are being mistaken for a hastening of good things; material increase is explicitly placed under suspicion.
terra: بَلْ لَا يَشْعُرُونَ denies that the supplied wealth is accelerated خَيْرَات, setting a boundary around what may be called true good.
terra: The garden's people have whatever they wish forever, and this is a promise charged to “your Lord”; it makes desired good a promised gift brought fully to its recipients.

luna: The worshippers pray that their spouses and offspring be “a comfort to our eyes.” This repeats the section’s eye-delight expression in a family setting and makes intimate joy one of the gifts sought from the Lord. | terra: The servants pray for spouses and offspring as قُرَّةَ أَعْيُنٍ; the source's dictionary expression for the eye's blessing becomes a requested family good.

luna: Pharaoh invokes the ordinary child-rearing sense of the section’s root ر ب ب, asking Moses whether “we raised you among us as a child.” His claim is later bounded by Moses’s return to his mother in 20:40, where Allah’s care completes the rescue Pharaoh’s household did not control. | terra: Pharaoh's أَلَمْ نُرَبِّكَ فِينَا وَلِيدًا uses the رب root of raising Moses as a child, furnishing the other concrete sense named in the source's opening distinction.
terra: Moses challenges Pharaoh's claim that raising him was a favor by pointing to Pharaoh's enslavement of Israel; it exposes the moral limit of calling child-rearing a benefaction.
terra: Abraham names the Lord who created him and guides him, beginning a first-person catalogue of care that moves through life's successive needs.
terra: Feeding and giving drink are the Lord's acts in Abraham's catalogue, supplying the provision stage of sustained divine care.
terra: “When I am ill, He heals me” contributes restoration to the same sequence, making care the repair of a damaged condition.
terra: Causing death and then giving life extends the Lord's care beyond present provision to the final change of state.
terra: Abraham hopes his Lord will forgive him on the Day of Judgment; the sequence ends in a hoped-for good whose completion lies in the later life.
terra: David and Solomon publicly praise God for knowledge and for favoring them; their speech is a direct model of telling a received favor.

luna: Sulayman asks to be enabled to thank the favor Allah bestowed on him and his parents, and to do a righteous deed that pleases Him. This directly joins the section’s favor, gratitude, goodness conveyed, and contentment. | terra: Solomon asks to be enabled to thank God for نِعْمَتَكَ الَّتِي أَنْعَمْتَ عَلَيَّ and to do a deed تَرْضَاهُ; received favor, gratitude, family extension, and divine approval meet in one prayer.
terra: When the throne appears, Solomon says هَذَا مِنْ فَضْلِ رَبِّي to test whether he will thank or deny; a received marvel is read as the Lord's favor and a summons to gratitude.

luna: Allah says He intends to favor those oppressed in the land, make them leaders, and make them inheritors. It is a specific staged reversal from low status to an enlarged favor, parallel to the section’s account of provision unfolding through stages.

luna: Following the promise in 28:5 to favor the oppressed and make them leaders and heirs, this ayah says Allah would establish them in the land and show Pharaoh and Haman what they feared. Its contribution is the promised favor’s concrete realization.

terra: God tells Moses' mother to nurse him, cast him into the river without fear, and trust the promise to return him and make him a messenger; the whole favor is announced from peril to its distant completion.

luna: Pharaoh’s wife calls the rescued infant Moses “a comfort of the eye for me and you.” The same child is eye-delight before his return to his mother in 28:13, adding an earlier household’s joy to the section’s return scene. | terra: Pharaoh's wife calls the infant قُرَّتُ عَيْنٍ لِي وَلَكَ, although the preceding ayah says he will become an enemy and grief to Pharaoh's house; eye-delight here carries an irony that marks the limit of present perception.
terra: God's preventing Moses from accepting other nurses allows his sister to direct Pharaoh's household back to his family; this ayah contributes the concealed mechanism completed in 28:13.

luna: This retelling says Moses was returned to his mother “so her eye might be comforted.” It repeats the section’s specific eye-delight scene and adds that she need not grieve and would know Allah’s promise was true. | terra: God returns Moses to his mother so that her eye may be comforted, she may cease grieving, and she may know God's promise is true; the eye's blessing arrives as a promise carried to completion.

luna: Moses says he is in need of whatever good his Lord may send down to him. The next ayah brings a man’s invitation and practical help; this one contributes the expressed need that makes the later provision a specific response.

luna: The section reads the Hereafter as better than the first life. This ayah says that what people have been given is worldly enjoyment, while what is with Allah is “better and more lasting,” sharpening the contrast between present possession and the better outcome. | terra: Worldly possessions are temporary enjoyment and adornment, whereas what is with God is better and more enduring; it directly restates the later-good comparison.
terra: One who meets a good promise is contrasted with one briefly given worldly enjoyment and then brought for judgment; fulfilled promise and passing gift are sharply separated.

luna: The section’s lexicon defines inʿām as conveying goodness to another. This ayah tells Qarun to do good as Allah has done good to him, making receipt of favor explicitly answerable by good directed outward. | terra: وَأَحْسِنْ كَمَا أَحْسَنَ اللَّهُ إِلَيْكَ turns goodness received from God into goodness delivered onward, directly realizing the source's definition of inʿām as conveying benefit to another.
terra: Qarun claims his wealth was given because of knowledge he possesses; the claim erases the giver and misreads accumulated good as self-produced.
terra: Those given knowledge tell the admirers of Qarun that God's reward is better for the faithful who do good; the claim corrects the crowd's reading of visible wealth.
terra: God causes the earth to swallow Qarun and his house, and no group or self-help can save him; apparent completion in wealth proves unable to preserve itself.
terra: The former wishers for Qarun's place now confess that God expands and restricts provision and that deniers do not prosper; the scene corrects its own false reading.
terra: Creatures unable to carry their own provision are provided for by God along with human beings; sufficiency is an ongoing act of the Provider, not self-possession.
luna: This ayah calls worldly life play and amusement and the Hereafter the real life. That is a specific boundary for the section’s claim that the later life is better than the first.
terra: Usury intended لِيَرْبُوَ in people's wealth does not increase with God, whereas alms seeking God's face are multiplied; the ayah distinguishes false increase from increase of conveyed good.
terra: Luqman receives wisdom with the charge to thank God, and gratitude benefits its practitioner; a received gift is answered by recognition.

luna: This ayah describes Allah as having “lavished His favors upon you, outward and inward.” The section presents the favor of the Lord as something completed and made known; the visible and hidden scope here shows how much that favor encompasses. | terra: God has subjected what is in the heavens and earth and أَسْبَغَ عَلَيْكُمْ نِعَمَهُ ظَاهِرَةً وَبَاطِنَةً; the verb depicts favors lavished or made ample, outward and hidden.

luna: The section’s dictionary expression for eye delight is echoed by the promised “comforts of eyes” hidden for people as recompense for their deeds. This locates eye-delight in a future gift whose full form remains unseen. | terra: No soul knows what قُرَّةِ أَعْيُنٍ has been hidden as reward; the eye's blessing is both future and concealed, fitting a good whose completion lies beyond present sight.
terra: Believers are commanded to remember God's favor when armies came and He sent wind and unseen forces; rescue under siege is another specific favor to be recounted.

terra: The Prophet's household arrangement is said to make the women's eyes comforted, remove grief, and leave them all وَيَرْضَيْنَ بِمَا آتَيْتَهُنَّ; eye-delight, a gift received, and satisfaction converge explicitly.

luna: The section’s dictionary definition for root ر ب ب includes making a good deed complete and sound. This ayah says Allah will set people’s deeds right and forgive them, a concrete parallel to soundness and completion of deeds.
terra: David's household is commanded to work in gratitude after the kingdom's extraordinary provisions, while few servants are grateful; thanks is an active use of favor.
terra: Sheba receives two gardens, abundant provision, and the command to thank a forgiving Lord; land, delivered good, and gratitude form a completed civic blessing.
terra: When Sheba turns away, the flood replaces the two gardens with bitter produce; the tended-land blessing is reversed through ingratitude.
terra: The reversal of Sheba's gardens is explicitly called recompense for ingratitude; it gives the reason for the loss narrated in 34:16.
terra: God says He expands provision for whom He wills and measures it, but most people do not know; expansion and restriction therefore cannot bear the honor/disgrace meanings assigned in 89:15-16.
terra: Neither wealth nor children bring people near to God; this supplies the explicit boundary missing from the mistaken prosperity reading.
terra: God expands and restricts provision, and whatever believers spend فَهُوَ يُخْلِفُهُ; good conveyed to others is met by the Provider's replacement.
terra: People are commanded to remember God's favor and asked whether any creator besides God provides from heaven and earth; narration of blessing leads to its sole source.
terra: Recitation, prayer, and spending from God's provision are called a commerce that will not perish; it supplies the acts whose reward 35:30 is paid fully and increased.

luna: This ayah says Allah will pay believers’ rewards in full and increase them from His bounty. It brings together the section’s two distinct actions—bringing a good to completion and increasing it—in one promise. | terra: لِيُوَفِّيَهُمْ أُجُورَهُمْ وَيَزِيدَهُمْ مِنْ فَضْلِهِ likewise places payment in full before increase from bounty, making completion open onto surplus rather than mere closure.
terra: God revives dead land and brings grain from it for people to eat; repaired earth is carried to an edible benefit.
terra: Gardens of palms and vines and springs opened within them develop the land-care scene begun in 36:33.
terra: People eat the land's fruit though their hands did not make it, and are asked whether they will thank; completed cultivation reaches another as provision and calls for gratitude.

luna: The section says riḍwān is abundant riḍā; this ayah says that if people are grateful, Allah approves their gratitude. Its contrast between human gratitude and ingratitude gives the section’s favor and contentment a reciprocal relation. | terra: God does not approve ingratitude, but وَإِنْ تَشْكُرُوا يَرْضَهُ لَكُمْ; gratitude and approval are explicitly joined, clarifying the response and endpoint of completed favor.

luna: This ayah says that the people of Paradise will have what they wish from their Lord, as reward for those who do good. It concretizes the section’s description of khayr as what is desired and the future gift that brings contentment.
terra: أَلَيْسَ اللَّهُ بِكَافٍ عَبْدَهُ asks whether God is not sufficient for His servant while opponents try to frighten the Prophet; divine sufficiency becomes protection amid hostile speech.
terra: After distress is removed and a favor is given, the person claims it came through personal knowledge; God calls it a trial, exposing false ownership of delivered good.
terra: Creation proceeds from dust and a drop through childhood, maturity, old age, and an appointed term; the ayah supplies an explicit state-to-state progression under divine agency.
terra: This repeated formulation says that a favored human turns aside arrogantly but becomes full of prayer under harm; changing conditions reveal an unstable reading of favor.

luna: This ayah distinguishes one who seeks the harvest of the Hereafter, whose harvest Allah increases, from one who seeks the harvest of this world and receives only some of it. It joins the section’s increase detail to its comparison of the two lives.
luna: The section’s entry for ن ع م notes a sense of increasing. This ayah says that whoever acquires a good deed will have goodness increased for him, a specific case of good being augmented.

luna: This ayah says that if Allah expanded provision for His servants, they would transgress, so He sends it down in a measure as He wills. It supplies a clear limit to reading abundance as a sign of honor, the mistake named in 89:15.

luna: This ayah says that what people have been given is worldly enjoyment, while what is with Allah is “better and more lasting” for those who believe and rely on their Lord. It restates the section’s khayr comparison with a specific contrast in what lasts. | terra: What people receive is temporary worldly enjoyment, while what is with God is better and more enduring for believers who trust Him.

luna: Addressing the Prophet, this ayah recalls that he did not know the Book or faith before revelation, then says Allah made the revelation a light by which He guides whom He wills. It is a specific parallel to the section’s movement from an earlier state to divine guidance.
terra: After being settled upon means of travel, people are commanded to remember their Lord's favor and declare His transcendence; ordinary provision becomes spoken remembrance.

luna: This ayah says Allah apportions livelihood and raises some people over others for mutual service, then says His mercy is better than what they gather. It makes provision a measured arrangement, not proof that worldly rank is the section’s final good. | terra: God apportions livelihoods and raises people in degrees, while وَرَحْمَتُ رَبِّكَ خَيْرٌ مِمَّا يَجْمَعُونَ; measured worldly provision yields to the Lord's better mercy.

luna: The section glosses “nuʿmatu al-ʿayn” as eye-delight; in this description of Paradise, “eyes delight” alongside whatever souls desire. It connects the section’s idiom to a final provision that meets both sight and desire. | terra: Paradise contains what souls desire and eyes delight in; satisfaction and the source's eye-delight sense meet in an enduring good state.

terra: At full maturity the servant prays to thank God for the favor given to him and his parents, to do work God approves, and to have his offspring repaired; favor is carried across a whole life and family.
terra: The clear victory is the concrete opening gift of the sentence whose next ayah says God's favor to the Prophet will be completed; it identifies one historical form of that completion.

luna: The section reads “bi-niʿmati rabbik” with the section’s dictionary sense of Rabb as one who brings a favor to completion. This ayah says Allah will complete His favor upon the Prophet and guide him to a straight path, joining completion to the stages of guidance visible in the surah. | terra: God joins completing His favor to the Prophet, وَيُتِمَّ نِعْمَتَهُ عَلَيْكَ, with guiding him on a straight path; this states outright the section's reading of the Lord who carries a favor through to guidance.
terra: God's mighty help completes the sequence of forgiveness, completed favor, and guidance in 48:2; the ayah contributes the protective support toward which the promise proceeds.
terra: God is pleased with the believers beneath the tree, sends tranquility upon them, and rewards them with a near victory; approval is accompanied by inward and outward gifts.

luna: The section describes favors unfolding step by step and cites care of land as a sense of root ر ب ب. This ayah’s seed sends out a shoot, strengthens, thickens, and stands upon its stem, a concrete progression from beginning to mature growth.

terra: Those who count their submission as a favor to the Prophet are corrected: بَلِ اللَّهُ يَمُنُّ عَلَيْكُمْ أَنْ هَدَاكُمْ; the direction and source of favor are reversed back to God and His guidance.

luna: This ayah says the people of Paradise will have whatever they wish and that Allah has “more.” It provides a specific image of provision exceeding desire, alongside the section’s account of the root ن ع م as increase. | terra: Paradise gives its people whatever they will, وَلَدَيْنَا مَزِيدٌ, and God still has more; fulfilled desire is followed by increase.

luna: This ayah repeats the section’s exact phrase “bi-niʿmati rabbik” while denying that the Prophet is a soothsayer or mad. Its own contribution is the paired rejection of accusations, showing the formula’s reassuring use in another passage. | terra: فَمَا أَنْتَ بِنِعْمَةِ رَبِّكَ بِكَاهِنٍ وَلَا مَجْنُونٍ repeats the exact phrase while clearing the Prophet of two accusations; favor here includes divine vindication.
terra: The question whether a human simply has whatever he desires sets a boundary on wish and entitlement; 53:25 answers that first and last belong to God.

luna: After asking whether a person has whatever he wishes, this ayah says the Hereafter and the first life belong to Allah. It repeats the section’s paired terms and locates the hoped-for good in the giver who owns both lives. | terra: فَلِلَّهِ الْآخِرَةُ وَالْأُولَى repeats the “later/first” pair and assigns both to God, preparing the following verse's statement about whom He wills and approves.
terra: Intercession is ineffective until God permits it for one He wills and يَرْضَى; as the continuation of 53:25, approval marks the boundary within God's ownership of first and last.

luna: The section describes the sixth-to-eighth ayat as shelter, guidance, and sufficiency, culminating in being enriched. This ayah names Allah as the one who enriches and grants sufficiency, giving a direct parallel for the last step in that progression. | terra: وَأَنَّهُ هُوَ أَغْنَىٰ وَأَقْنَىٰ attributes both enrichment and lasting contentment to God, directly paralleling the sufficiency granted in 93:8 and its movement toward satisfaction.

luna: The section’s dictionary definition of completing and improving a good deed is made perceptible by this question: “Is the reward of ihsan anything but ihsan?” It joins a well-done good act to its fitting return.
terra: “Have you seen what you sow?” supplies the human act whose completion 56:64 assigns to God, establishing the field scene needed by the source's estate-tending dictionary form.

terra: أَأَنْتُمْ تَزْرَعُونَهُ أَمْ نَحْنُ الزَّارِعُونَ assigns the crop's actual growth to God; it gives the source's dictionary image “رَبَّ الضَّيْعَةَ,” tending an estate to completion, a Quranic scene.
terra: God could turn the crop into dry debris after people sow it; this continuation of 56:63-64 marks the dependence and reversibility of a cultivated blessing.
terra: The goodly loan is promised multiplication and a noble reward; generosity opens into increase from God.
terra: Men and women who give charity and lend a goodly loan receive multiplication and noble reward; the repeated formula applies increasing good to both.

luna: This ayah describes worldly life as play, adornment, boasting, and competition in wealth and children, then contrasts its brief growth and decay with the Hereafter. It illuminates both 93:4’s preference for the later life and 89:15’s mistaken reading of worldly plenty. | terra: Worldly life is pictured as vegetation that pleases and then withers, while the Hereafter holds punishment, forgiveness, and riḍwān; transient increase is set against enduring approval.

luna: This ayah says people should not grieve over what escapes them or exult over what Allah gives, then warns against boastful pride. It directly limits the false reading in 89:15–16 that worldly increase or restriction by itself signifies honor or humiliation.
terra: A goodly loan is multiplied and joined to forgiveness; increase and repair complete the good passed onward.
terra: Whoever relies on God finds فَهُوَ حَسْبُهُ; God reaches His purpose and has set a measure for everything, so sufficiency is presented as care that unfailingly reaches its appointed end.

luna: The section’s phrase “bi-niʿmati rabbik” recurs exactly in this denial that the Prophet is mad. The same favor formula serves as assurance against slander, clarifying that recounting the gift in 93:11 rests on the Prophet’s divinely given standing. | terra: مَا أَنْتَ بِنِعْمَةِ رَبِّكَ بِمَجْنُونٍ repeats the section's exact phrase and makes the Lord's favor the ground on which slander against the Prophet is denied.

luna: The section defines inʿām as delivering goodness to someone else. This ayah stages that transfer as feeding the needy, orphan, and captive, turning an abstract favor into provision that reaches particular people.

luna: The feeders say that they give only for Allah’s countenance and seek neither repayment nor thanks. That adds a distinct motive to the section’s command to recount Allah’s favor: giving can be directed to God without seeking return from its recipients.

luna: This ayah names the contrary preference, that people choose the nearer life; 87:17 supplies the section’s own boundary by saying the Hereafter is better and more lasting. Its contribution is the human preference that the comparison corrects. | terra: بَلْ تُؤْثِرُونَ الْحَيَاةَ الدُّنْيَا names preference for the nearer life as the error to which 87:17's “Hereafter is better and more lasting” responds.

luna: The section’s word خَيْر says the Hereafter is better than the first life; this ayah says “the Hereafter is better and more lasting.” It adds endurance to the section’s comparison of the two lives. | terra: وَالْآخِرَةُ خَيْرٌ وَأَبْقَى repeats the section's central comparison almost exactly and adds that the better later life also remains.

luna: This ayah uses the section’s root ن ع م in “He made him comfortable,” after expanded provision; the person then concludes “my Lord has honored me.” The next ayat challenge this reading, showing a false equation of comfortable circumstances with honor. | terra: A person receives honor and comfort yet says رَبِّي أَكْرَمَنِ; the ayah stages the section's false reading that material expansion by itself proves divine honor.

luna: This ayah contributes the opposite misreading: when provision is restricted, the person says his Lord has humiliated him. Its own claim is about constriction; 89:15 supplies the paired claim from plenty, and 89:17 turns from both claims to actual conduct toward the orphan. | terra: When provision is measured tightly, the same person says رَبِّي أَهَانَنِ; alongside 89:15 it exposes the opposite but equally false equation of provision with worth.

luna: After the claims in 89:15–16 that plenty means honor and restriction means humiliation, this ayah answers “No”; it names failure to honor the orphan as the real fault. It connects the section’s definition of inʿām as conveying good to another with the surah’s own care for the vulnerable. | terra: كَلَّا rejects those readings and immediately points to failure to honor the orphan; the truth of favor is tested in whether received good is passed to the vulnerable.

luna: This continuation identifies another failed transfer of goodness: people do not urge one another to feed the poor. The section’s dictionary gloss for inʿām is conveying good to someone else, so the ayah’s concrete provision of food exposes what mere worldly increase fails to accomplish. | terra: Failure to urge feeding the poor continues the correction of 89:15-16 and mirrors the social obligation that follows remembered sufficiency in surah 93.
terra: Devouring inheritance greedily shows abundance consumed rather than transmitted as good, completing the ethical diagnosis around the false claim of honor.
terra: Excessive love of wealth identifies the attachment behind the mistaken reading of plenty as completed favor.
terra: The “tranquil soul” is the addressee invited to return well pleased and pleasing in 89:28; inner settledness introduces the section's true endpoint of satisfaction.

luna: The section links divine completion to contentment; this ayah describes the soul returning to its Lord “well-pleased and pleasing.” It gives contentment as the completed end of a life, followed in the next ayat by entry among Allah’s servants and into His garden. | terra: The addressed soul returns رَاضِيَةً مَرْضِيَّةً; genuine completion ends in reciprocal satisfaction, in contrast with the unstable judgments about wealth in 89:15-16.
terra: Entering among God's servants is the first realized outcome after the soul is called well pleased and pleasing.
terra: Entering God's garden completes the sequence begun with the tranquil soul, locating satisfaction in the final bestowed home.

luna: This ayah describes one who withholds and considers himself self-sufficient. It reverses the section’s step in which Allah finds the Prophet in need and makes him sufficient: here apparent self-sufficiency accompanies refusal to give.

luna: In the surah that later describes a giver who seeks Allah’s face and becomes satisfied, this ayah says the Hereafter and the first life belong to Allah. It repeats the section’s paired terms and frames both outcomes as belonging to the Lord. | terra: وَإِنَّ لَنَا لَلْآخِرَةَ وَالْأُولَى places both the later and the first with God; it repeats 93:4's two temporal terms and opens the movement that reaches satisfaction in 92:21.
terra: The person promised eventual satisfaction in 92:21 gives wealth for purification; the ayah shows conveyed good as the action within the promise's movement.
terra: Seeking only the face of his Lord gives the giver's stance immediately before “he will surely be pleased”; satisfaction is oriented to the Lord rather than repayment by people.

luna: The section’s root ر ض و names the Prophet’s contentment after a future gift. Here the one who gives wealth to purify himself and seeks his Lord’s countenance in 92:18–20 “will surely be satisfied”; the same contentment is reached through a distinct act of giving. | terra: وَلَسَوْفَ يَرْضَى nearly answers 93:5's وَلَسَوْفَ ... فَتَرْضَى word for word; here the promised satisfaction completes the story of one who gives wealth seeking only his Lord.
terra: The question “Have We not expanded your breast?” begins another divine enumeration addressed to the Prophet, continuing the form of remembered care used in 93:6-8.
terra: “We removed from you your burden” contributes release from a former state to the neighboring enumeration of favors.
terra: The burden “which weighed upon your back” identifies the distress repaired by 94:2, making the favor a concrete change of condition.
terra: “We raised for you your remembrance” completes the neighboring sequence with an increased public good granted to the Prophet.

luna: The section describes the Prophet’s life as moving through distinct states before a future gift brings contentment. This ayah gives a specific promise of ease accompanying hardship, which illuminates the transition from need and vulnerability toward sufficiency.

luna: This ayah repeats the preceding promise that ease accompanies hardship. Its contribution is the second assurance in 94:5–6, reinforcing the section’s movement through successive states toward a good outcome.
terra: كَلَّا إِنَّ الْإِنْسَانَ لَيَطْغَى warns that the human being transgresses, and the next ayah locates the trigger in imagined self-sufficiency.
terra: أَنْ رَآهُ اسْتَغْنَى makes seeing oneself as self-sufficient a cause of rebellion, reversing 93:8's sufficiency received from God.

luna: The section links riḍwān to full contentment; this ayah joins gardens to Allah’s approval of the believers and theirs of Him. Its own contribution is the reciprocal approval named as the reward of those who fear their Lord. | terra: Eternal gardens culminate in “God is pleased with them and they are pleased with Him”; reciprocal approval is the fullness of the promised good state.
terra: God tells the Prophet that He has given him al-Kawthar, an abundant good; it is a direct fulfilled counterpart to the Lord's promise to give in 93:5.
terra: The command to pray and sacrifice to one's Lord follows the abundant gift in 108:1, modeling an enacted response after favor has been announced.
